title: From the glass slide to foundation models
subtitle: Selected milestones in computational pathology. The axis is compressed before 2000. Hover or tap a marker for details.

events.label: Cellular pathology
events.detail: Rudolf Virchow argues that disease is a disorder of cells, which makes the microscope the center of diagnosis.

events.label: H&E
events.detail: Hematoxylin and eosin are combined into the stain still used on most diagnostic slides (usually dated to the 1870s).

events.label: Antibody labeling
events.detail: Coons and colleagues label tissue antigens with fluorescent antibodies, the ancestor of immunohistochemistry.

events.label: Gleason grading
events.detail: Donald Gleason codifies prostate cancer architecture into patterns, still the basis of prostate grading.

events.label: First cell-image analysis
events.detail: Prewitt & Mendelsohn publish 'The analysis of cell images', classifying blood cells by computer.

events.label: Automated Pap screening
events.detail: The first automated cervical cytology screening systems reach the U.S. market in the mid-1990s.

events.label: DICOM for WSI
events.detail: DICOM Supplement 145 defines a standard for whole-slide images.

events.label: WSI for primary diagnosis
events.detail: The FDA authorizes a whole-slide imaging system for primary diagnosis in the U.S.

events.label: Remote sign-out
events.detail: Pandemic-era waivers allow U.S. pathologists to review cases remotely, accelerating digital adoption.

events.label: First AI authorization
events.detail: Paige Prostate becomes the first AI pathology product authorized by the FDA (De Novo, September 2021).

events.label: C-Path
events.detail: Hand-crafted image features of breast cancer stroma predict survival (Beck et al., 2011).

events.label: Deep nets find mitoses
events.detail: Deep convolutional networks win the ICPR 2012 mitosis detection contest (Cireşan et al., 2013).

events.label: U-Net
events.detail: A convolutional encoder–decoder designed for biomedical segmentation.

events.label: CAMELYON16
events.detail: Algorithms detect breast cancer metastases in lymph nodes as well as an unhurried pathologist (published 2017).

events.label: Mutations from H&E
events.detail: Networks predict lung adenocarcinoma mutations from routine H&E slides (Coudray et al., 2018).

events.label: Weak supervision at scale
events.detail: Multiple-instance learning on 44,732 slides with only diagnosis labels (Campanella et al., 2019).

events.label: CLAM
events.detail: Data-efficient attention-based multiple-instance learning with interpretable heatmaps.

events.label: PANDA
events.detail: A global Gleason grading challenge on 10,616 prostate biopsies with 1,290 developers.

events.label: PLIP
events.detail: A vision–language model trained on 208,414 pathology image–text pairs shared on medical Twitter.

events.label: UNI · CONCH
events.detail: Self-supervised (UNI) and vision–language (CONCH) foundation models for pathology.

events.label: Prov-GigaPath
events.detail: A whole-slide foundation model pretrained on 1.3 billion tiles from 171,189 slides.

events.label: Virchow · CHIEF · PathChat
events.detail: A 1.5-million-slide model, a weakly supervised pan-cancer model, and a multimodal generative copilot.

events.label: DINOv3 · TITAN
events.detail: Meta's DINOv3 general-purpose vision backbone; TITAN, a multimodal whole-slide model trained on 335,645 slides.
